title: Affective Music Recommendation: A Rollout-Based World Model for Offline Preference Optimization
domain: Affective music recommendation and digital therapeutics
dataset_or_cohort: Proprietary LUCID clinical and consumer-wellness interaction logs
sample_scale: 939 users; 8,784 sessions; 57,822 interactions; 5,992 unique songs played from a 6,988-song catalog; 16,927 positive and 2,561 negative ratings
institution_count: Single platform; clinical site count NI
split_strategy: Ten random Monte Carlo splits, 80/10/10 by user ID; users disjoint and splits shared across models
observation_process: Irregular song-level engagement and optional ratings plus session-level pre/post valence-arousal under a fixed production policy
missingness: Ratings and post-session affect are optional; losses mask unobserved positions; no imputation reported
censoring_or_competing_events: Session endings observed; dropout or informative censoring NI
state: Listening history containing songs, feedback and session boundaries
observation_decoder: Predicts engagement, rating, valence and arousal feedback
action_provenance: Historical songs selected by the deployed production policy; imagined songs selected by evaluated policies
transition_mechanism: Factorized causal decoder-only transformer; predicted feedback is appended autoregressively
rollout_regime: Free-running song-feedback rollout initialized from logged histories
capability_claim: Closed-loop offline preference optimization and predeployment simulation; real-user causal efficacy is not demonstrated
baselines: Architecture and embedding ablations; Random, Greedy and Copycat policies; no independent simulator
state_fidelity_metrics: Continuous feedback MSE and R2; rating AUC
transition_metrics: Rollout-level predicted feedback only; no horizon-stratified transition error
rollout_stability: Coverage, normalized entropy, intra-list diversity, Gini and policy alignment across rollouts
action_sensitivity: Recommended-song-input removal plus Random, Greedy, Copycat and DPO policy comparisons; no action shuffling or dose response
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI; no predictive intervals, coverage or calibration analysis
external_validation: None; one proprietary platform and logged policy
decision_utility: Simulator-predicted DPO valence-arousal and diversity gains; no online patient or user outcomes
safety_evaluation: Fully offline evaluation, Copycat and KL anchoring, diversity and alignment monitoring, and synthetic or perturbed-history stress tests; no deployment hazard protocol
statistical_analysis: Ten split mean and SD with paired t-tests; policy evaluation uses five shared random seeds
causal_language: Uses counterfactual-history and in-silico-simulator language without causal identification
estimand: Model-predicted feedback and utility under dynamics learned from the logged production policy; not an intervention effect
confounding_strategy: Exposure bias is acknowledged and behavior-cloning or KL regularization is used; no measured-confounder adjustment
positivity_and_overlap: NI; action support or overlap is not evaluated
counterfactual_validation: NI; perturbed histories are stress tests rather than ground-truth counterfactuals
data_access: Private proprietary logs; no public data access
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial; embeddings, sequence construction, masked losses and split procedure are described, but the full production preprocessing pipeline is unavailable
randomness: Ten random user splits and five shared policy seeds; exact seed values NI
evidence_anchors: p.1 Abstract; pp.2-4 Sec. 3 and Fig. 1 for data, state, action and model; pp.5-8 Sec. 4 and Tables 1-5 for splits, metrics, ablations and policy rollouts; p.8 Sec. 5.1-5.3 for safety scope and limitations
appraisal_strengths: User-disjoint cold-start evaluation, repeated splits and seeds, missing-aware objectives, and several rollout diversity or stability measures
appraisal_limitations: Optimization and evaluation use the same learned simulator; single platform and policy; no calibration, external validation, online outcomes or causal identification

title: Brain-WM: Brain Glioblastoma World Model

institution_count: Five named dataset sources; exact clinical site count NI

observation_process: Irregular longitudinal 3D FLAIR, T1CE and T2W MRI with demographics and cumulative treatment history
censoring_or_competing_events: Loss to follow-up, death and competing events NI

observation_decoder: Generates the next 3D MRI and predicts the next treatment token
action: Specified next treatment category: surgery, radiotherapy, chemoradiotherapy, temozolomide or other medication
action_provenance: Recorded clinical treatment for training; candidate treatment supplied for conditional generation
transition_mechanism: Y-shaped mixture-of-transformers with shared latent representation, autoregressive treatment branch and latent flow-matching MRI branch using 50 Euler steps
maximum_horizon: One observed next clinical timepoint; interval analyses include greater than 360 days
rollout_regime: Single-next-timepoint treatment-conditioned prediction, not recursive longitudinal rollout
capability_claim: Claims a counterfactual sandbox for care optimization; evidence supports observed-policy next-treatment classification and conditional one-step MRI synthesis
baselines: VLM and medical-VLM planning baselines; AliFuse and Hyperfusion; LE-DUNet, LE-GAN, IL-CLDM, LDM-GBM, MedWM and TaDiff
state_fidelity_metrics: MRI NMSE, PSNR and SSIM; qualitative tumor masks; treatment accuracy, F1, specificity and precision
transition_metrics: Pearson correlation of predicted versus observed tumor-volume change by interval and treatment; no recursive trajectory metric
rollout_stability: NA; recursive multi-step rollouts are not evaluated
action_sensitivity: Treatment-stratified correlations only; no treatment removal, shuffling or matched alternative-action test
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI; aleatoric uncertainty is discussed but not quantified or calibrated
external_validation: Independent RHUH-GBM and UCSD-PTGBM cohorts totaling 61 subjects
decision_utility: Retrospective agreement with clinician treatment plans and future MRI; no prospective clinical outcome or decision study
safety_evaluation: No hazard, override or failure-management evaluation; risk-free-sandbox wording is not empirically established
statistical_analysis: Point estimates and correlations are reported; CIs, significance testing and repeated seeds NI
causal_language: Uses counterfactual, co-evolution and causal-dependency language
estimand: Observed next-treatment and next-MRI association conditional on recorded history; no identified treatment-effect estimand
confounding_strategy: No confounding adjustment; pseudoprogression is acknowledged as a limitation
positivity_and_overlap: NI; treatment overlap is not assessed
counterfactual_validation: None; no ground-truth outcomes under unchosen treatments
code_access: Public GitHub repository linked in the paper
data_access: Five named research datasets; access follows their source terms
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial but substantial; metadata extraction with manual verification, skull stripping, SRI24 registration, 192 x 192 x 140 cropping, intensity scaling and augmentation are described
randomness: Random 8:2 split and augmentations; seed values and repeated training runs NI

appraisal_strengths: Subject-level splitting, two independent external cohorts, strong task-specific baselines and explicitly treatment-conditioned images
appraisal_limitations: No causal assumptions or counterfactual validation, no multi-step rollout, calibration, safety or prospective utility; dense within-patient pairs may overweight some subjects

title: DreamReg: Belief-Driven World Model for 2D-3D Ultrasound Registration

split_strategy: CAMUS official split; micro-RegPro case-level 7:1:2 split
observation_process: Synthetic 2D slices rendered from 3D ultrasound volumes along pose trajectories rather than a live intraoperative stream
missingness: NA for the constructed slice-volume pairs; no missing-data process is modeled
state: Stochastic latent state, recurrent belief, current pose and 3D volume context
observation_decoder: Decodes imagined 2D slices, progress reward and final 6-DoF pose
action_provenance: Policy-generated at inference; synthetic expert trajectories with noise perturbations are used for training
transition_mechanism: Dreamer-style Gaussian prior and posterior with recurrent latent transition
maximum_horizon: Seven steps for CAMUS and five for micro-RegPro
rollout_regime: Posterior-conditioned training; free-running closed-loop imagination at inference without new observations

baselines: CUReg, EUReg and FVRNet; pose-only, no-reward and no-reconstruction ablations
state_fidelity_metrics: Image dissimilarity error, image NCC and SSIM
transition_metrics: Translation error, rotation error, pose NCC and frames per second
rollout_stability: Final-horizon registration is reported; no stepwise drift, constraint-violation or failure-probability analysis
action_sensitivity: Synthetic pose perturbations up to plus or minus 10 and model-component ablations; no action shuffle
calibration_and_uncertainty: Stochastic latent state is used, but predictive calibration or coverage is NI
external_validation: A second public anatomy dataset tests cross-domain generality; no independent live center or device validation
decision_utility: Registration accuracy and 40-56 FPS runtime; no clinician, robot or patient study
safety_evaluation: No hazard analysis, safe-action constraints, fallback or override evaluation
statistical_analysis: Mean and SD are reported; CIs, hypothesis tests and repeated-seed details NI
causal_language: Action-observation coupling and imagination language; no treatment-causal claim
estimand: Geometric registration pose and image alignment
confounding_strategy: NA; action is a synthetic geometric transformation rather than treatment assignment
counterfactual_validation: Physics-based slice rendering constrains geometry, but no empirical counterfactual validation is provided
code_access: Public project or code page linked
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial but detailed; resampling, synthetic slicing, trajectories, perturbations and fixed test sets are described
randomness: On-the-fly pose perturbations are random; fixed evaluation sets are used; seed values NI
evidence_anchors: p.1 Abstract; pp.3-6 Sec. 2 and Figs. 1-2 for state, actions and dynamics; pp.6-8 Sec. 3 and Tables 1-2 for datasets, horizons, metrics and ablations; p.9 Conclusion
appraisal_strengths: Case-level splits, two datasets, genuinely free-running inference, and geometric, image and runtime metrics
appraisal_limitations: Evaluation uses resampled synthetic slices, omits tissue deformation and live feedback, and lacks rollout-drift, calibration, safety and repeated-seed analyses

state_fidelity_metrics: NA; observations are not reconstructed for fidelity evaluation
transition_metrics: Failure-detection rate, false-alarm rate, nonconformity-score traces and 13.98 Hz runtime
rollout_stability: Endpoint-horizon ablation from one to four steps; no long-rollout drift analysis

calibration_and_uncertainty: Conformal calibration at alpha 0.05 using 19 successes per task and episode-peak thresholds; exchangeability is required and sample size is small
external_validation: Both simulation and real dVRK hardware tasks are included; no clinical surgical validation
decision_utility: Offline detection of failures; no online interruption, recovery or patient-benefit evaluation
safety_evaluation: Failure modes are detected offline, but no online stop, recovery, override or harm-severity protocol is evaluated
statistical_analysis: Aggregate episode counts and rates are reported; CIs, significance tests and repeated seeds NI
causal_language: Nominal-consistency language; no causal treatment-effect claim
estimand: Failure-alarm performance under the evaluated imitation-policy distribution
counterfactual_validation: NA; no alternative-action outcome ground truth
code_access: Planned for release upon acceptance; unavailable at inspection
weights_access: Planned for release upon acceptance; unavailable at inspection
data_access: Planned for release upon acceptance; unavailable at inspection
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial but detailed; image resizing, DINO features, beta-VAE compression, windows and thresholds are specified
evidence_anchors: p.1 Abstract; p.2 Fig. 1; pp.3-4 Sec. III for states, actions and flow model; pp.4-6 Sec. IV and Table I for tasks, calibration and counts; p.7 Figs. 5-6 for action and horizon ablations; p.8 Limitations
appraisal_strengths: Disjoint conformal calibration, simulation and real hardware, 20 diverse failure modes and explicit action ablations
appraisal_limitations: Training-demo scale is NI; evaluation is offline with only 19 calibration successes per task and no CIs, seeds, online intervention or clinical validation

title: medDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning with Latent Imagination on Complex EHRs for Clinical Decision Support
domain: ICU electronic health records and offline treatment reinforcement learning
dataset_or_cohort: MIMIC-IV sepsis cohort and eICU mechanical-ventilation cohort
sample_scale: 21,233 adults with sepsis and 21,595 ventilation patients aged at least 16 years
institution_count: MIMIC-IV is single-center; eICU is multicenter, exact site count NI
split_strategy: NI; the inspected primary text does not establish patient-level train, validation and test construction
observation_process: Irregular sparse vitals, labs and demographics with elapsed-time and observation masks; sepsis spans 24 hours before to 48 hours after onset and ventilation up to 14 days
missingness: Informative missingness is represented through an AFI module; reconstruction losses use masks and do not backpropagate through missing observations
censoring_or_competing_events: Exclusions include multiple stays and treatment withdrawal; a continuation head models episode continuation, but formal censoring or competing-event handling is NI
state: Stochastic latent patient state inferred from values, masks and elapsed time
observation_decoder: Reconstructs observations and predicts reward and continuation
action: Sepsis: 25 fluid-vasopressor combinations; ventilation: 18 PEEP, FiO2 and tidal-volume combinations
action_provenance: Recorded clinician treatment in real trajectories; actor-selected treatment during imagination
transition_mechanism: GRU prior-posterior latent world model with actor and critic

rollout_regime: Free-running latent imagination after posterior initialization, with hybrid real-to-imagined training variants

state_fidelity_metrics: Only qualitative multivariate reconstruction examples; no comprehensive variable-by-horizon fidelity table
transition_metrics: No direct transition-error evaluation; WIS, WPDIS, CWPDIS, ESS and return assess policy outcomes rather than learned dynamics
rollout_stability: Imagination-length and hybrid-grounding ablations; no physiologic-drift or constraint-violation analysis
action_sensitivity: Treatment-distribution, clinician-agreement and dose-difference analyses; no action-removal or shuffled-action test
calibration_and_uncertainty: Estimated mortality has reported 95 percent CIs, but this is not predictive calibration; sepsis point estimates and CI text or table appear internally inconsistent
external_validation: Two large independent EHR datasets and tasks are studied, but no frozen train-one-cohort test-another-cohort transport validation
decision_utility: Estimated mortality from off-policy evaluation; no prospective treatment assignment or patient outcomes
safety_evaluation: Hybrid grounding and clinician-final-control discussion; no deployment hazard, fallback or override test
statistical_analysis: Estimated mortality CIs are reported; seed count and formal between-method significance details NI
estimand: Claimed policy outcome or mortality under alternative treatment policies, but the estimand and identification assumptions are not formally specified
confounding_strategy: No measured-confounder strategy beyond behavior-policy learning and off-policy evaluation
positivity_and_overlap: NI; treatment-policy support and overlap are not quantified
counterfactual_validation: None; no ground-truth outcome under unchosen treatment
data_access: Credentialed research access to MIMIC-IV and eICU
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial; eligibility, windows, features and action discretization are described, but split construction and full executable preprocessing are NI
evidence_anchors: pp.1-3 Abstract and Introduction; pp.3-8 Sec. 3 for observations, missingness, actions, latent dynamics and imagination; pp.8-13 Sec. 4, Tables 1-2 and Figs. 2-8 for cohorts, OPE, ablations and treatment analyses; pp.18-19 appendices for ethics and feature definitions
appraisal_strengths: Two large EHR cohorts, explicit informative-missingness modeling, long free-running imagination, several OPE estimators and useful ablations
appraisal_limitations: Patient splits are NI; dynamics validation is weak; confounding, overlap and censoring are not addressed; mortality benefits rely on OPE; reported sepsis CIs require adjudication
reviewer_confidence: High; especially verify split reporting and mortality CI inconsistency
